title: Evaluating models against your own set of cases

videos.script: This is the lesson that outlives every model in the course. A benchmark measures somebody else's work. Only your own cases measure yours. {{cases}} So you write them: forty real e-mails, each with the label a person chose, and a rule for what counts as right. Exact, or tidied first. Valid JSON, or something a person would accept. {{harness}} A short program sends every case to every candidate and keeps every answer. {{scores}} Then you read the scores honestly. Thirty out of forty sounds precise. With forty cases it means somewhere between sixty and eighty-six per cent. {{pairs}} The sharper question is which model wins on the same cases. Sixteen to five happens by chance about three times in a hundred. {{failures}} Then the failures, which tell you what kind of mistake each model makes: a list where one label belongs, an order number nobody wrote, a refusal. {{gate}} Last, you keep the run, and you let a program refuse any change that makes it worse.
